title: Is there a reason to own both MV and MZ?

posts.author: GuardianofRidgewood
posts.body: The Steam summer sale is on at the moment and I can pick up RPG Maker MV for about $11. I do already own RPG Maker MZ though so I'm hesitant to make the purchase. Can anyone tell me if there might be any benefits to owning both MV/MZ together or if I should just stick with MZ since I already have it? Any advice would be helpful.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: A couple. Like having access to the default assets that come with both engines. Or making a game in MV to take advantage of the cheaper, probably still bigger plugin library, but using MZ for mapping since it has that layer control.

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Imagine RMMV to be the biggest resource pack you could ever buy. Cause it does not just allow you to use all the resoures that come with it (and that is a lot, plus it has e.g. really pretty battlebacks you can mix and match with MZs), but also all the free community resources that require you to own RMMV, like

posts.author: GuardianofRidgewood
posts.body: Awesome. Thank you for the replies. I'll definitely take advantage of the sale and pick up MV.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body: It may not apply to you, but there are some devs who prefer using MV, but do their mapping using the MZ editor.  As an MZ owner who is using MZ, I am very happy I bought MV.  It allows me to not worry about which one assets were made for in the store and also applies to modded graphics made available online by others.  This is the reason I also picked up XP and VXAce which go on sale frequently.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
There are two reasons I own them both.
1.  As mentioned above... you can freely use the resources from one engine into another.  You can't do that without owning both engines (it's in their TOS and other such places).  This includes sprites, tilesets, monsters, battlebacks, etcetera.  This is pretty useful to get more things "in the style of the RTP" if you like that style, because they basically never sell any DLC in the same style (aside from maybe tilesets).
2.  Each engine has its own quirks and limitations.  It can sometimes be fun to try to make the same game in two engines and see how you have to work around some limitations or how things in other ways have gotten easier.  As an example, my main/primary project started in VX Ace, but it moved into MV when I was allowed to define "equipment slots".  As in, not just rename existing ones, but create new ones altogether.  My game doesn't function without this feature, so I had to primarily move it in there... or get a plugin to make it work with VX Ace.
There is also a reason I own all the RPG Maker engines.
As silly as it is, I have a baseline game from the same "universe" in each engine.  My secondary game is actually being created in RPG Maker 2000 (this is the one I work on when I get stuck or need to think pretty hard about my primary game).  I like doing this because it is also a representation of how the "world" has changed within the universe, and it allows me to tell different stories more easily.

posts.author: shIxx
posts.body:
The use of resources is a big reason as mentioned above.
Second reson is that MV is running on Linux if you plan to release for Steam Deck

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: For me the main reason is the RTP (default graphics), if you have both of them, you can use both graphics in any of them, which is very useful for me personally (using MV graphics in MZ).

posts.author: Aesica
posts.body:
Definitely worth getting MV if you already have MZ.
- MZ has really ugly default A1-A5 assets compared to MV.
- MV has a good amount of bonus content in its dlc folder.
- You can try making games in MV with a better plugin selection that won't break the bank.
- If you want to use sprite-based skill animations, MV is basically an asset pack for those.
- MV was from the pre-paypig era, so there's a lot more stuff available for it for free.
- MV has Harold!

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
You might find that some plugins for MV work on MZ without hassle.
I am an MV user. I am trying out MZ on my new laptop, which is currently misbehaving with both RPG Maker MV and MZ to the extent that it is just possible to use them. I tried an MV plugin called "PD_AdjustSprites" on MZ, and it works!
PD_AdjustSprites makes the party and most other sprites smaller on overworld maps.
